To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the BCS theory of superconductivity is applicable to neutron star matter, that it is possible to extend the BCS theory to include effects of the medium and of retardation of interactions, and that the BCS-BEC crossover can be realized in dilute nuclear matter.

the BCS mean-field theory is a good description of pairing in nuclear matter at zero temperature, that the BCS-BEC crossover is a generic feature of dilute nuclear systems, that the superfluid proton component of neutron stars is a type-II superconductor with the vortex state being in the London limit, and that the superfluid neutron component is a type-I superconductor.

1) The pairing gap in neutron stars is strongly affected by the medium polarization and the retardation of the pairing interaction; 2) The pairing interaction in the neutron star interior is strongly enhanced by the medium polarization; 3) The proton pairing is weak and is suppressed by the Coulomb interaction, which is, however, partially compensated by the medium polarization effect; 4) The proton pairing can become strong in the vicinity of a phase transition from a neutron to a proton superconductor
In summary, our research is concerned with
the physics of superconductivity, superfluidity, and magnetism in nuclear systems, including dense neutron matter and neutron stars.
the study of the properties of the superfluid state of nuclear matter, in the framework of the BCS model and its extensions, in the case of neutron star cores.
the physics of superconductivity in neutron star interiors, with the aim of developing microscopic and phenomenological models that can be tested with observations.
